automated.summary: All 8 required leaves executed and passed under the vitest discriminator (testcase present in the junit report, not <skipped/>, not <failure/>) - the discriminator matters because vitest exits 0 and marks unmatched leaves skipped (D-0031). Task 1's fifteen leaves pass with their bodies byte-identical; selection-identity.helper.test.ts is untouched, and the only deletions in use-ask.test.tsx are in the shared Harness fixtures adapting to AskTurn.response now being optional while a turn is pending, which criterion c2 requires. 17 tests green across the two task-1 files. verify.py passes. Live on this worktree (backend :4000, frontend :3000): three in-app Open cycles each reached /ask within 80ms of the click - navigate-first, c1 - with cycle 0 appending exactly one turn (unmatched, c2) and cycles 1-2 reusing that same turn so the thread length stayed at 1 (matched, c3, and the duplicate-turn bug this story exists to fix); the target turn was in view after every cycle (c4). The pending turn was measured directly by holding /api/chat open: it renders 'Opening this report...' at 11px slate, matching its sibling status lines. Design pass (both mandatory skills genuinely applied, not merely attested) found two real defects, both fixed and both re-measured live: the pending status line rendered 16px near-black - the loudest text in the thread for a transient loading state - because .ask-period-status has exactly one rule and it is the DESCENDANT selector '.ask-answer .ask-period-status', which a single element carrying both classes does not match; extending that rule to '.ask-answer.ask-period-status' took it 16px ink -> 12px ink -> 11px slate, each step measured with getComputedStyle on the real element. And the progress copy said 'Reopening report...' after a control labelled 'Open', so the action changed verbs mid-flow; it now reads 'Opening this report...'.
